title: Count errors in logs that aren't all UTF-8

blocks.text: Every night the operations team counts the error lines in each host's log. Most hosts write UTF-8; the old warehouse hosts write ISO-8859-1, and `countAnyCharset` already reads a log again in that charset when it isn't valid UTF-8. Logs live on a network mount, so now and then a read fails, and `scan` already skips such a log and reports why. Last night the whole batch stopped at the first warehouse log, and the logs after it were never counted.
Finish `count(log, charset)` in `src/main/java/practice/ErrorCounter.java`. It reads the log with `BufferedReader.lines()` and counts the lines the team's `Rule` calls errors.

When you're done, a warehouse log is counted in its own charset, a log that can't be read is reported as skipped while the rest of the batch is counted, and a broken `Rule`, which is a bug for its team to fix, still stops the batch. About six lines in total.
The tests hand the counter logs that live in memory; they decode, and fail, the way `Files.newBufferedReader` does.

cases.says: each UTF-8 log gets the number of lines the rule calls errors, and nothing is skipped
a log that can't be opened is skipped with the exception that opening it threw, and the next log is counted
a log written in ISO-8859-1 is counted, not skipped
a log whose read fails part-way is skipped with that read failure, and the next log is counted
an exception thrown by the rule itself stops the batch instead of marking the log skipped

origin.section: Streams Can't Throw IOException, So Files.lines Throws UncheckedIOException from the Terminal Operation

concepts: Files.lines and BufferedReader.lines throw read errors as UncheckedIOException from the terminal operation, past a catch for IOException; unwrapping getCause() restores the IOException.
